model: Managed-care FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: equity 5yr CAGR 5.81% cross-checked against nominal US health-spending growth (~5-6%); revenue CAGR (10.3%) is inflated by low-margin CarelonRx pass-through revenue and FY2024 acquisitions and is not a profit-growth proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.8% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 10.3% and from EPS 3yr CAGR 1.0%. Revenue growth outpaced earnings because the mix shifted toward CarelonRx pharmacy revenue (near-pass-through margins) and because Medicaid/ACA margins collapsed in FY2024-25; EPS has been flat for three years.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; investment income NOT stripped because no cash is credited outside the flows). Both the reported and owner series show ~-20%/yr over 5 years, but FY2020 was a COVID claims-deferral OCF peak (10.7bn) and FY2025 an OCF trough on Medicaid receivable timing (4.3bn), so the FCF CAGRs describe cash timing, not earnings power -- net income was 4.6bn in FY2020 and 5.7bn in FY2025. Owner-FCF CAGR is ~1pp below reported because SBC+withholding has held ~300m while FCF fell. Anchors: revenue FY2020 121,867 -> FY2025 199,125; EPS 18.23 -> 25.28; equity 33,187 -> 44,026; owner FCF 9,256 -> 2,866; 3yr from FY2022 (156,595 / 24.56 / 36,330 / 6,890).

scenario_narratives.base: Trough-and-recover: FY2026 Medicaid (-1.75%) and MA (~2%) margins mark the bottom; rate adequacy and repricing restore a 4.3% pre-tax margin by FY2030 as Carelon lifts revenue 5-6%/yr. Value is the FCFE stream at an 8.5% cost of equity with a 15x exit, no net-debt deduction (debt service is in the flows, regulated capital is not surplus).
scenario_narratives.bull: Regulatory overhang clears (sanction lifted, Medicaid rates reset, ACA pool stabilises) and Carelon compounds into an Optum-like services engine; pre-tax margin back to the FY2022 5.2%, revenue +6.5-7.5% through FY2030, 16x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Washington risk crystallises: MA enrolment freeze, Medicaid/ACA cuts shrink membership, medical trend keeps beating rate-setting; margin stuck at the FY2025 trough (3.4%), revenue growth below health-spending inflation, 13x exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Elevance is valued as an equity stream: FCFE (pre-tax earnings after interest, taxed at a normal 24%, plus D&A, less capex and a tuck-in M&A allowance) discounted at an 8.5% cost of equity, with the terminal value capped at a sector-typical 13-16x FCFE. No net debt is deducted and no cash is added: the debt is serviced inside the flows and the cash and investment portfolio are regulated statutory capital. SBC is expensed and the share count held flat, so the 2.6bn/yr buyback is the return of FCFE, not a value driver of its own. The single judgment the valuation turns on is whether the pre-tax margin recovers from the FY2025-26 government-programs trough (3.3%) toward 4.3% -- each 0.5pp of mature pre-tax margin is worth roughly $55-60/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pre-tax margin recovery does not materialise: Medicaid rate adequacy lags acuity for another cycle, MA margins stay ~2%, and the FY2025 3.4% becomes structural (the bear case, ~30% weighted).
CMS Medicare Advantage sanction (unauthorised risk-adjustment data submissions 2018-25) escalates to a prolonged enrolment freeze or civil penalties.
Federal Medicaid cuts and ACA eligibility/subsidy overhaul shrink covered lives and adversely select the remaining pool.
Reserve (IBNR) understatement -- a repeat of the 2024-26 industry-wide guidance resets.
Cost of equity: at 8.5% the Gordon multiple (17x) already exceeds the 15x cap, so value is bounded by the cap, but each +1pp on the rate is worth roughly -$40/share (see required_return_table).
D&A is partly estimated (only intangible amortisation of 628 is XBRL-tagged); this affects the EBIT/add-back split, not FCFE.
Y1 anchor: FY2026 GAAP EPS floor of $20.10 implies a weak H2; if the H2 charges are larger than modelled the Y1 FCFE of ~$4.5bn is overstated by up to ~$0.9bn, worth ~$4/share of PV.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 274.84-436.24
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1156039): FY2025 10-K and Q1/Q2 2026 10-Qs for pre-tax income, tax, interest expense, intangible amortisation, diluted shares, debt, cash, investments; ELV_Metrics.csv (106 periods) for revenue/NI/OCF/capex/SBC/equity history; kpis table for buybacks and equity-award taxes
data_sources.qualitative: ELV_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Q2 2026 guidance (adjusted EPS >= $27.00, GAAP >= $20.10, OCF >= $6.0bn, MA margin >= 2%, Medicaid ~-1.75%, FY2027 >= 12% EPS growth), CMS sanction timeline, Carelon growth, bull/bear axes

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation 276 + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 32 (no combined figure published; SBC is NOT excluded from Elevance's adjusted EPS, so house and street bases nearly coincide)
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 2,605; H1-2026 1,358 (kpis). Dividends 1,529 FY2025, $1.72/qtr = $6.88/yr. Count is falling ~3%/yr; held FLAT here because SBC is expensed in the flows and the buyback cash is the mechanism that keeps it flat -- the excess repurchase above SBC is the shareholder's FCFE being returned, already counted once in the flows.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares Q2 2026 10-Q (217.9m); cover-page basic count 216.87m at 2026-07-10 plus ~0.9m dilutive awards. Held flat (SBC expensed).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are FCFE (post-interest). USD build: 10y UST ~4.2% + 0.85 beta x 5.0% ERP = 8.5%. Managed-care betas run 0.6-0.8 but the 2024-26 guidance-reset volatility and Washington policy dependence argue for the top of the range. Single rate across all three scenarios -- scenario risk is carried in the probability weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial for a health insurer (right-of-use assets <0.5% of assets); lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the pre-tax margin. No separate lease line, no lease liability in debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests immaterial (<$50m of equity); flows are attributable to Elevance shareholders.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: net_debt held at ZERO by design. Total debt 31,419 (30,669 LT + 375 current + 0 short-term at 2026-06-30, XBRL) and interest expense of ~1.4bn/yr are already inside the pre-tax flows; deducting the debt again would double-charge it. Cash 10,232 and the 28.5bn investment portfolio (AFS debt 26,978 + equity securities 1,563) are statutory capital held in regulated insurance subsidiaries against ~17bn of medical claims payable and RBC requirements -- they are not surplus and are not added back. Net investment income (2,194 FY2025) is the return on those reserves and stays in the flows; the matching-asset rule is satisfied because neither the income nor the asset is credited outside the flows.
inputs.ebitda_mapping: ENGINE MAPPING: ebitda_margin_path = (pre-tax income AFTER interest expense + D&A + SBC) / revenue, so the engine's EBIT equals GAAP pre-tax income, NOPAT equals net income, and the engine's 'owner FCF' equals FCFE. FY2025 actual: pre-tax 6,710 + D&A ~1,500 + SBC 276 = 8,486 / 199,125 = 4.26% (depressed by ~650m of below-the-line investment losses and optimisation charges). H1-2026 actual pre-tax 4,241 on revenue 100,655 = 4.21%, but Q3/Q4 are seasonally weak (FY2025 Q4 pre-tax was 215m).
inputs.da_note: Intangible amortisation 628 (XBRL AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets FY2025). Total D&A including capitalised-software and PP&E depreciation is not separately tagged; estimated at ~1,500 (0.75% of revenue), consistent with 1.1-1.3bn/yr of capex. D&A is added back in the engine, so this estimate only affects the split between EBIT and the add-back, not FCFE.
inputs.capex_note: PP&E + capitalised software capex 1,116 FY2025 (0.56% of revenue). capex_pct is set at 1.0%: 0.55% sustaining capex plus a 0.45% allowance for the tuck-in acquisitions that fund the Carelon growth embedded in the revenue path (FY2024 acquisitions 4.8bn: Paragon, Kroger Specialty Pharmacy, CareBridge; FY2025 ~0; BCBS Louisiana pending). Prior-deal amortisation is added back through D&A, new-deal spend is charged here -- each charged once.
inputs.wc_note: wc_capture_pct = 0. For a health insurer the growth in medical claims payable (float, ~10% of premium) is offset by statutory capital that must be retained in the regulated subsidiaries as premium grows (RBC). FY2019-23 OCF ran ~1.5x net income on float growth; FY2024-25 OCF ran below net income on Medicaid receivable timing. Over a cycle the two net to roughly zero, so neither is credited.
inputs.tax_note: FY2025 effective rate 15.6% (1,049 / 6,710) is abnormal -- FY2024 24.5%, H1-2026 24.2%. Cash tax rate modelled at 24% from year one; the FY2025 benefit is not perpetuated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Managed-care FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity via the Drivers/engine route (same family as IAG.AX). WHY NOT BVPS-compounding (the SKILL.md insurer default): Elevance does not compound book -- it returns ~75% of earnings through buybacks (2.6-2.9bn/yr) and dividends (1.5bn/yr); book value grew 5.8%/yr over 5 years while ROE ran 13-17%, so a P/B exit would value the payout stream at zero. WHY NOT owner-FCF at WACC less net debt: the 10bn cash and 28.5bn investment portfolio are regulated statutory capital, not surplus, so 'net debt' is undefined -- deducting gross debt without the cash is far too punitive and netting the regulated cash is far too generous. FCFE at cost of equity sidesteps that by keeping interest expense and investment income both inside the flows and setting net_debt = 0. FY0 = FY2025 (last full year); Y1 = FY2026, three quarters complete (Q2 10-Q is the latest filing; Q3 reports late October 2026). FY2026 guidance (Q2 release): adjusted EPS >= $27.00, GAAP EPS >= $20.10, OCF >= $6.0bn, MA operating margin >= 2%, Medicaid operating margin ~ -1.75% (trough), >= 12% adjusted EPS growth in FY2027. The GAAP-adjusted gap (~$6.90/share, ~1.9bn pre-tax) is intangible amortisation plus optimisation charges and investment losses; the Y1 pre-tax margin of 3.3% (~6.6bn) sits between the GAAP floor (5.7bn) and the adjusted figure (7.7bn), giving weight to the 4.2% H1 run-rate net of Q3/Q4 seasonality. Price is the 2026-09-25 regular close (Friday); valuation date is the following Monday, not an after-hours print.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: pre-tax margin 2.9 -> 3.0 -> 3.2 -> 3.3 -> 3.4% flat -- the FY2025 trough becomes the new normal, plus D&A 0.75 and SBC 0.15.
bear.narrative: The CMS sanction becomes a multi-year MA enrolment freeze plus civil penalties; the 2025 reconciliation bill's Medicaid cuts and ACA eligibility overhaul shrink covered lives and adversely select the exchange pool; medical trend (GLP-1s, behavioural, outpatient) keeps outrunning rate-setting so the 2024-26 guidance-reset pattern repeats. Membership keeps eroding, revenue grows 2.5-3.5% (below health-spending inflation), and pre-tax margin never recovers past 3.4%. Exit at 13x FCFE, the multiple the sector carried through 2024-25.

base.ebitda_margin_note: pre-tax margin 3.3 -> 3.7 -> 4.0 -> 4.2 -> 4.3% flat, plus D&A 0.75 and SBC 0.15. Mature 4.3% is below the FY2021-24 average (4.9%) because of the CarelonRx mix shift; recovery path follows management's FY2027 >=12% EPS growth target and the Medicaid/MA margin normalisation from the FY2026 trough.
base.narrative: FY2026 is the government-programs margin trough (Medicaid ~-1.75%, MA ~2%); revenue +1.5% on membership attrition. FY2027-29 Medicaid rate adequacy catches up with acuity, MA repricing holds a 3-4% margin, and Carelon external growth lifts revenue 5-6%/yr with pre-tax margin recovering to 4.3% -- short of the FY2021-24 4.9% average, reflecting the lower-margin pharmacy mix. Terminal value capped at 15x FCFE (Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would be 17.1x), the sector's long-run earnings multiple.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: pre-tax margin 3.5 -> 4.1 -> 4.6 -> 5.0 -> 5.2% flat (back to the FY2022 level), plus D&A 0.75 and SBC 0.15.
bull.narrative: CMS lifts the MA enrolment sanction with no further penalty; Medicaid rates reset to acuity in the 2027 cycle; ACA risk pool stabilises after the subsidy overhaul; Carelon (revenue +33% in FY2025) keeps compounding external clients and CareBridge value-based care lifts the services margin -- the Optum playbook a decade behind. Pre-tax margin returns to the FY2022 5.2% by FY2030 and revenue grows 6.5-7.5% through FY2030. Exit at 16x FCFE.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the downside is a single-regulator dependency (CMS sanction unresolved since March 2026, Medicaid and ACA funding set in Washington) and management's cost-trend visibility failed three times in 2024-26. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- the sanction lifted cleanly, Medicaid rates resetting to acuity, the ACA pool holding after the subsidy overhaul, and Carelon's external growth sustaining -- and each is outside management's control. Base 50%: the FY2026 trough-year framing is consistent with the Q2 guidance raise, and a partial margin recovery is the modal outcome.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
